entries.location: Potion chamber — bottle selection and passage
entries.description: The riddle specifies three poisons, two nettle wines and two passage-enabling drinks; wine has poison on its left side as worded, end bottles differ, neither end leads onward, smallest/largest are safe, and second from each end taste alike. Hermione identifies the tiny smallest bottle for black fire and a rounded bottle at the right end for purple fire. The cold-tasting drinks allow her to retreat and Harry to enter the last chamber unburnt.
entries.model_notes: Positions of smallest and largest within the line are not numbered in the prose; do not invent them. The smallest bottle has only one swallow left. The riddle’s left-side statement should be preserved as a puzzle constraint, not a complete bottle map.

entries.description: Divination is at the top of North Tower, a long journey estimated by Ron at ten minutes. After seven long staircases the trio reach an unfamiliar stone-walled landing with a painting; an empty passage branches right and a window gives a partial lake view. entries.model_notes: Seven flights are not seven floors. South is Ron’s orientation claim tied to the lake sightline, not an independently surveyed bearing.

entries.location: Entrance Hall Goblet and Age Line
entries.description: The Goblet stands in the centre of the Entrance Hall on the stool normally used for the Sorting Hat. A thin golden circle is marked on the floor ten feet around it in every direction. Dumbledore says under-seventeens cannot cross; Fred and George’s Ageing Potion fails and the line ejects them onto the cold stone floor ten feet away, giving them white beards. Names dropped into the Goblet briefly turn its blue-white fire red and produce sparks.
entries.model_notes: Preserve both the stated ten-foot extent around the Goblet and the separately stated ejection distance. Neither should be silently converted into a ten-foot diameter. The age restriction is explained and then observed.

entries.description: Harry and Ron leave via the Entrance Hall and open front doors, descend the steps, and follow winding ornamental paths among rose bushes, large stone statues and carved benches. Splashing first suggests a fountain; farther along they see tall sparkling jets beyond a large stone reindeer and a stone bench facing the water.
entries.model_notes: The fountain is initially heard and subsequently observed. Bushes, shadows and the reindeer screen people from one another while voices remain audible. Beetle presence is transient.

entries.description: The bathroom is made of white marble and softly lit by a candle-filled chandelier. A rectangular swimming-pool-sized bath is sunk into the centre of the floor, surrounded by roughly a hundred golden taps with differently coloured jewels in their handles; it has a diving board. Long white linen curtains cover the windows, fluffy white towels are piled in a corner, and footsteps and the egg’s cry reverberate off the marble.
entries.model_notes: The water is deep enough that Harry’s feet barely reach the bottom, and the pool permits swimming lengths. These are relative scale constraints, not numeric measurements.

entries.location: Lake ascent and landing after second task
entries.description: Harry ascends through darkness which lightens near the surface, noticing daylight about ten feet above as Gillyweed expires. On surfacing the hostages awaken; they swim back to the judges’ bank escorted by about twenty merpeople. Pomfrey treats the rescued competitors on shore with blankets and Pepper-Up, and later leads them uphill back to the castle steps.

entries.model_notes: The ten-foot figure is the final surface clearance, not total lake depth. The lethal deadline was Harry’s misunderstanding; Ron says safeguards prevented drowning.

entries.location: Maze Cup approach and spider damage
entries.description: At a later fork Harry follows the wand-guided right-hand path and sees the gleaming Cup on a plinth a hundred yards ahead. Cedric joins from another route. A gigantic spider visible over the left hedge advances along an intersecting path; it lifts and drops Harry twelve feet, then combined Stunning Spells topple it sideways, flattening a hedge and filling the path with tangled legs. The Cup is only feet from Cedric after the fight.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Preserve local crossing, final straight view, plinth and temporary hedge damage. The twelve-foot fall is not a measured spider height.

entries.description: On arrival Harry sees dark shop fronts, black mountains beyond the village, the curve in the road ahead leading towards Hogwarts, and light from the Three Broomsticks. They retreat from the High Street into the nearest narrow side street.
entries.model_notes: Local street curve and mountain backdrop without compass bearing. Three Broomsticks functions as a Death Eater base that night.

entries.description: Their night arrival causes a piercing scream, which a Death Eater silences with his wand. The Death Eaters call it a Caterwauling Charm enforcing curfew; Aberforth says moving outdoors in darkness triggers it and that curfew lifts at daybreak.
entries.model_notes: Observed alarm plus attributed explanation. The alarm detects an outdoor presence despite the Invisibility Cloak; it does not itself identify the trio’s exact position.

entries.description: The trio cannot Disapparate: the air feels solid. Dementors draw light from the surroundings and stars, bring intense cold, and approach around a corner of the side street, ten or more appearing darker than the darkness. A Patronus drives them away and the stars return.
entries.model_notes: Dated town restriction and environmental effect, not proof of permanent year-round town anti-Apparition rules.

entries.location: Hog’s Head side entrance → upstairs sitting room
entries.description: A bolted door opens on the left side of the narrow street into the Hog’s Head’s grubby, sawdust-strewn bar, lit by one flickering candle. Behind the counter a second doorway leads to a rickety wooden staircase opening into the upstairs sitting room.
entries.model_notes: Tunnel access approach; relative left is from the trio’s retreat, not a compass direction. The upstairs grimy window overlooks the street.

entries.location: Hog’s Head upstairs sitting room / tunnel anteroom
entries.description: The sitting room has a threadbare carpet, small fireplace, wobble-legged chair and a small table before the fire. One large oil painting of a blonde girl hangs above the fireplace; it is the room’s only picture. A small rectangular mirror stands on the mantelpiece directly below it. Harry closes the window curtains; Aberforth lights lamps and the fire.
entries.model_notes: Necessary model context for tunnel mouth. Mirror is a communication object, separate from the passage portrait; no Albus photograph is present.

entries.description: Aberforth advises waiting until daylight, leaving Hogsmeade on foot and climbing into the mountains, where Apparition becomes possible. He reports Hagrid hiding in a cave there with Grawp after the attempted arrest.
entries.model_notes: No surveyed town boundary, cave coordinates or identity with the earlier mountain cave supplied.

entries.location: Hog’s Head Ariana portrait / real tunnel entrance
entries.description: Ariana’s painted figure walks away into a long dark tunnel depicted behind her, then returns with Neville. The whole picture swings forwards like a little door, revealing a real tunnel. Neville climbs out and jumps down from the mantelpiece.
entries.model_notes: Portrait aperture is above the fireplace/mantelpiece; the painted approach depicts the real tunnel’s traveller. Far endpoint and dimensions await the next chapter.

entries.location: Hogwarts boundary walls / old passages / patrols
entries.description: Aberforth reports all old secret passages watched at both ends, Dementors around the boundary walls, and regular patrols within the school; he says his alternative is now the only way in.
entries.model_notes: His sources support a very heavily guarded wartime state; “only” is his assessment, not a guarantee against every magical exception.
